record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.original_question: Extend the same ant-inspired reinforcement model from finite graphs to the two-dimensional integer lattice Z^2 with a nest N and food vertex F: do the reinforced random walks asymptotically identify geodesic edges, in the sense that only edges on shortest N-to-F paths have weights growing linearly?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 Prove the main conjecture on Z 2 .
the only edges whose weight will grow linearly are those lying on a geodesic between N and F.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following ant-inspired edge-reinforced random walk model on the two-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with its nearest-neighbor edge set $E$. Fix two distinct vertices $N$ (the "nest") and $F$ (the "food"). Assign to every edge $e \in E$ an initial positive weight $w_0(e) > 0$. Successive "ants" are sent out one at a time, indexed by $n = 1, 2, \dots$.

At step $n$, the $n$-th ant performs a random walk starting at $N$: at each vertex $v$, it jumps along an incident edge $e$ with probability proportional to the current weight $w_{n-1}(e)$, continuing until it first reaches $F$. (One may consider either the trace of the forward path, its loop-erasure, or the geodesic in the trace between $N$ and $F$ as the "reinforced" set of edges, in analogy with the corresponding variants studied on finite graphs.) Each edge belonging to the reinforced set of the $n$-th ant's trajectory has its weight increased by $1$, producing the new weight function $w_n$.

A path from $N$ to $F$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is called a geodesic if it has minimal length $\|N-F\|_1$ among all $N$-to-$F$ paths.

Question: Prove that, almost surely, an edge $e$ satisfies $\liminf_{n\to\infty} w_n(e)/n > 0$ if and only if $e$ lies on some geodesic from $N$ to $F$. Equivalently, show that asymptotically only edges on shortest $N$-to-$F$ paths have weights growing linearly in $n$, while all other edges have sublinear weight growth.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that ant-inspired reinforced random walks identify geodesic edges is studied on finite graphs (e.g., series–parallel graphs, triangle-series-parallel graphs), but its extension to $\mathbb{Z}^2$ remains an open problem. Recent work (Kious–Mailler–Schapira and subsequent papers up to 2024–2026) addresses variants on finite graphs and shows that some reinforcement schemes (e.g., trace-reinforced) do not find shortest paths, while the loop-erased and geodesic variants are conjectured to. No proof on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is reported.

status_evidence.title: The trace-reinforced ants process does not find shortest paths
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that the trace-reinforced variant fails to find shortest paths in general; motivates studying loop-erased/geodesic variants.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates ongoing investigation of reinforcement variants and shortest-path identification; the $\mathbb{Z}^2$ case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The two-nest ants process on triangle-series-parallel graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ant reinforcement on finite graph classes, leaving lattice cases as open conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the conjecture remains active on finite graph families with $\mathbb{Z}^2$ unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The ants walk: finding geodesics in graphs using reinforcement learning
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the conjecture that reinforced ant walks find geodesics, currently proved only on certain classes of finite graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Supports the status that the $\mathbb{Z}^2$ version is an open conjecture.
